exposure: Timing of diagnosis and treatment for Cesarean scar pregnancy (first trimester vs. later in pregnancy)
outcome: Complications (transfusions, massive bleeding, urinary or vascular complications)
Type of management required (multiple management types, cesarean section, emergency hysterectomy)
cohort: Twelve patients diagnosed with Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP).
finding: Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) diagnosed and treated later in pregnancy resulted in significantly more severe complications, including massive bleeding, transfusions, and emergency hysterectomy, compared to those treated in the first trimester.
